quizName: DMV Practice Test #9 25 Questions • Passing Score 21

questions.question: Most motorcycles have:

options.text: Brakes on both the front and rear.
Three brakes: front, rear, and emergency.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brakes on both the front and rear.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have two brakes—one for the front wheel and one for the rear wheel.

questions.question: The body generally eliminates how many alcoholic drinks per hour?
questions.explanation: The body can eliminate about one drink per hour on average. This varies from person to person. Never drive after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Signal, check your mirrors, and turn your head.
Turn your head and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check your mirrors, and turn your head.
questions.explanation: Always signal before changing lanes. Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to see if it is safe to change lanes.

questions.question: As a beginning rider, when following another vehicle you should:

options.text: Keep at least a four-second distance behind them.
Not worry about your following distance.
Always ride on the left side of your lane so they can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep at least a four-second distance behind them.
questions.explanation: Beginning riders should keep at least a four-second distance from the vehicle ahead. Increase this distance in bad weather or poor road conditions.

questions.question: If one of your tires goes flat while riding, you should:

options.text: Gently brake with the tire that is not flat.
Go faster to leave the road quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gently brake with the tire that is not flat.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, ease off the throttle and stay straight as you slow down. If you need to brake, gently use the brake on the tire that is not flat.

questions.question: Most crashes happen:
questions.explanation: Most crashes happen on trips shorter than five miles, just a few minutes after the rider starts out.

questions.question: A motorcyclist is best protected when wearing:

options.text: A jacket that exposes the arms.
Shoes that stop below the ankle.

questions.explanation: Wear a jacket and pants that cover your arms and legs fully. Wear tall, sturdy boots that cover and support your ankles. Use low-heeled boots that will not catch on pegs or the road. Leather gloves protect your hands and give you a better grip on the controls.

questions.question: If hazards are on your left, you should ride:

options.text: In the left portion of the lane.
In the right portion of the lane.
In any portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the right portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: When hazards are on your left, ride in the right portion of the lane. Be ready to change your position as road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: The front brake provides about how much of a motorcycle's stopping power?
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: When stopping, you should:

options.text: Apply both brakes at the same time.
Use only the front or rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes whenever you slow down or stop. Apply them together at the same time.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle with a sidecar, where should the passenger sit?

options.text: Either on the motorcycle or in the sidecar.
Neither on the motorcycle nor in the sidecar.

questions.explanation: If your motorcycle has a sidecar, your passenger should ride in it. They should keep their hands inside the sidecar at all times.

questions.question: Which of the following should NOT be true of an effective face shield?

options.text: Allow clear views to both sides.

questions.explanation: A good face shield should be free of scratches, allow clear side views, fasten securely, and let air pass through. An airtight face shield can fog up and make it hard to see.

questions.question: What should your lane position do for you?

options.text: Minimize your space cushion and allow you to be seen by others.
Maximize your space cushion and allow you to be seen by others.
Maximize your potential for encountering road hazards and allow others to pass you.
Minimize your potential for encountering road hazards and allow you to closely follow another vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Maximize your space cushion and allow you to be seen by others.
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that gives you more space around you and helps others see you. This position helps you avoid wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. It also discourages other riders from sharing your lane and gives you an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: What should you NOT check during your pre-ride inspection?
questions.explanation: Before riding, check your tires, oil and fluid levels, headlight, taillight, turn signals, brake light, clutch, throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: If there are only a few vehicles on the roadway.
If drivers are following the speed limit.

questions.explanation: Increase your distance behind other vehicles if the pavement is slippery, if you cannot see past the vehicle ahead, or if traffic is heavy. Your motorcycle will need more space to stop safely.

questions.question: Why is a flat front tire especially dangerous?

options.text: The front tire provides power, so you will lose acceleration.
The flat tire will shake the bike, making it hard to use the mirrors.
You won't be able to use the brake.

questions.explanation: A flat front tire is dangerous because it affects your steering. If your front tire goes flat while riding, safely exit the road as quickly as possible.

questions.question: How should a group of motorcyclists ride through a curve?
questions.explanation: When riding through curves, turns, entering a highway, or leaving a highway, switch from a staggered formation to a single-file formation.

questions.question: When should you use both brakes to slow or stop?

options.text: Only if the pavement is wet.
Only when riding in the city.

questions.explanation: Using both the front and rear brakes gives you the most stopping power. Use both brakes every time you slow or stop.

questions.question: What is a benefit of a shatter-resistant face shield?

options.text: Can protect a rider's face in a crash.
Is only useful in protecting riders from dirt.
Does not offer as much protection as goggles.
Should not be used with a helmet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can protect a rider's face in a crash.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face during a crash. Goggles protect only your eyes. A face shield also protects from dirt, dust, insects, rain, and pebbles.

questions.question: When is it important to flash your brake light?

options.text: You will be slowing where other drivers won't expect it.
There is a stop sign ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will be slowing where other drivers won't expect it.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle brake lights are harder to see than larger vehicle brake lights. Flash your brake light when slowing down unexpectedly, such as in the middle of a block or near an alley.

questions.question: Many over-the-counter drugs:

options.text: Only affect your riding if you drink alcohol while taking them.

questions.explanation: Like alcohol, many drugs (including prescription drugs, over-the-counter drugs, and illegal drugs) can have side effects that make it harder to ride safely.

questions.question: The best source of information about your motorcycle is:
questions.explanation: The owner's manual has the most important information about your specific motorcycle. Read it before you ride for the first time.

questions.question: Crashes happen most often to:

options.text: Riders who know their motorcycle well.
Riders who have taken a safety course.

questions.explanation: Crashes happen most to new riders who have not had training and do not know their motorcycle.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to weave over rain grooves or bridge gratings, you should:

options.text: Steer side to side to match the weave.
Stay calm, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
Move to the left side of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay calm, keep a steady speed, and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles may weave over rain grooves or bridge gratings, but this is usually not dangerous. Stay calm and ride straight at a steady speed. Trying to weave with your motorcycle will make things worse.

questions.question: Riding between two vehicles moving in the same direction:

options.text: Is okay if traffic is heavy.
Is okay during the day to reduce traffic.
Is okay if you feel comfortable doing it.

questions.explanation: In Oregon, it is illegal for motorcycles and mopeds to pass between two moving vehicles on a highway with multiple lanes or on a one-way street.
